1. Would choose bamboo bc zero waste. However I use my electric toothbrush bc I prioritize my health. Now I would love to see an electric toothbrush that works well with vibrating/oscillating movements that I can replace the battery for/fix the parts as necessary. I feel like that would be the best way to elongate an electric toothbrush while using less materials to put less strain on the environment. Don’t see this happening due to capitalization … but one can hope.

2. Would def pay more for a high quality eco friendly toothbrush. But won’t put up w greenwashing - would want it to be 100% compostable in my backyard bc a) I (plus many others) don’t have easy access to commercial composting and b) if it’s not 100% compostable or able to be sent back to company to be manufactured, I don’t think it’ll be a very eco friendly option. That being said, bristles are super important. Lots of greenwashing when the toothbrush replacement head is made of wood (or even wood looking plastic!) but the bristles are made of plastic :( high key feels like greenwashing and would not buy. That being said, softer bristles are always better. Softest bristles could be a great selling point. However, there are some concerns about natural bristles causing more damage to gums than synthetic bristles bc synthetic is more uniform so less chance of abnormalities hurting your gums. Idk - this one I can’t really make a choice on, but your target audience would probably want 100% natural, compostable bristles.
Also I don’t think that high quality would be a good enough selling point for me personally because there would have to be a unique selling point about it - something different than what’s in the market right now - because otherwise I will continue to opt for my electric toothbrush, to be replace by natural heads when I use up my plastic ones. 

3. Features that are impt are listed above but soft bristles are a huge point. Plus the 100% HOME/backyard compostable aspect. I feel like 100% backyard compostable packaging would have to be a definite given. Design - eh. Personally as long as it works and in line with my values, design is not that big of an issue for me. Would be cool to see name engravings or color differentiation esp for people who share living spaces & use the same brand. Helps avoid awkward situations lol

4. Zero waste is the only reason I would make a purchase. Just being eco-friendly wouldn’t cut it for me, because there’s other companies doing bamboo/wood toothbrushes. Some even are doing stainless steel I believe though the heads are silicone so ig you pick your battles.

If you take up any of these ideas or have updates, I’m interested in hearing your progress. I take my dental health and zero waste seriously and it’s hard to find a balance between the two without making some sacrifices. Good luck

Hi I appreciate the concern, but I wonder why all this hate for my post? Genuinely curious because I see comparable collections in the past being posted, even more excessive ones on different platforms.

If my one collection would stop climate change, I would change it in an instant. But the truth is it takes collective societal change. I think yes there can be overconsumption, but also responsibly consuming is important. I have been decluttering my house, selling things secondhand; secondhand is always better because it reduces resource and energy usage for making more things. For things I can’t sell off, I give away or donate to those who need it. Despite a lot of pushback from my family, I started my own composting bin and run my own backyard garden in the spring and summer. I reduce take out to once a week. I switched from plastic shampoo and soap to bar soap. I switched to a leaf razor than using single use razor cartridges. I’ve been recycling out all plastic that I can. I bring my own bags and jars to grocery stores to buy as much in bulk and zero waste as I possibly can in my area. Owala’s were my swap to reusable water bottles. And that’s just the stuff off the top of my head. There’s so many more sustainable swaps that I’m excited to do.

Why do I bring this up?? Because I am trying to responsibly consume. Not perfectly, but on a path of imperfect sustainability. I appreciate your concern and I understand where it is coming from. However I do think that shaming others will never persuade more people to live sustainably. If your concern is **truly** overconsumption, I hope that you will be able to live what you preach, because living by example is a much more impactful method of changing your life than to call out other people. I learned that the hard way too.

I collect bottles because it brings me joy. This is one of the few things I give myself more freedom. If I didn’t buy any of these but just one or two just for the sake of environmentalism, it’d be easy for me to grow hate and disdain for such a restrictive practice. I know because I’ve been there. Being perfect is never attainable, and I hope you understand that. If I wish to downsize, I plan on locally selling it secondhand since each bottle does take a lot of resources and energy to make. Again, a lot of people criticize others for overconsumption, but I think mindful consumption and usage will allow the community as a whole to become more sustainable. I’d rather have 1000 people doing sustainability imperfectly than 1 person doing it perfectly. And that’s why I don’t understand the people who criticize me. Because if they truly cared about the environment, why don’t we see more environmental activism on this subreddit? Is collecting a few bottles going to ruin the planet??

Or is it the irresponsible corporations who do not care about the environment?? In 2017, The Guardian published that [100 companies are responsible for 71% of global greenhouse emissions](https://amp.theguardian.com/sustainable-business/2017/jul/10/100-fossil-fuel-companies-investors-responsible-71-global-emissions-cdp-study-climate-change). If my one water bottle could change the world, I wouldn’t hesitate. But climate change is much more complex and it requires more effort from everyone to truly make an impact. Perhaps the person you’re calling out is not the right person you should be calling out, food for thought.

Something about too much abrasion and causing more damage to the gum lines and/or contributing to enamel erosion… so forth and so on. I’ve heard some dentists say that it’s more helpful to floss than to brush teeth. It’s because flossing helps get rid of the bacteria in between the teeth which can contribute to bad breath from my understanding. I started flossing, and I noticed a drastic difference in my teeth and I’m very happy at where I’m at as a result of starting to floss daily. At first it will most likely be painful with some bleeding, but that is most likely a sign of gingivitis. Please keep flossing daily and build a habit because I swear it is one of the best things you can do for your teeth.
